questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The specialisation of the receiving university motivated me to spend 2 semesters there. In Göttingen the Focus was on Forests in a changing climate, the other options that presented themselves were less appealing to me. Moreover, the University of Göttingen is rated among the Top Universities in Europe in the field of forestry. The international network such as the quality of research there were additional reasons for my decision to go there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The fact that a lot of my classmates also chose to spend their second year in Göttingen made it really easy for me establish a healthy study/life balance. The size of the city was also very conducive for regular get togethers.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think our programme was very well structured. I am also familiar with the study environment in Germany, so i did not encounter big problems upon arrival. Thanks to the status as erasmus student i received a spot in an affordable student dorm in Göttingen. The orientation phase was very smooth and i think we had a seamless transition to the actual teaching period.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No physical assistance, but as i said we were prioritised for the student accommodation, and that was very helpful and easing for the mind.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got a place through the Studierendenwerk. Me and all of my classmates that went that way received a spot in a student appartement. I can only recommend this for Erasmus students in the future.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Göttingen is not a very big city, therefore it does not really matter where you live since everywhere is rather close to campus, and the public transportation is usually reliable. I can however recommend, to get a bike in Göttingen since you are faster and more flexible around the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Newly renovated and super affordable, i would have given 6/5

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: For my program it is pretty straight forward, since we only had one restricted elective module, that we could choose out of a pool of 3 options. First you sign up for the courses  at the beginning of the lecture period, sometimes there are deadlines, or passwords for course contents, so that you have to at least attend some of the lectures. The actual registration for the exams starts later, and then it is important to register. Usually it is being advertised regularly by the lecturers, and the process is also not very complicated.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Asking classmates i guess, for me there was no help required, so i can not answer properly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% I got all the courses i wanted, and i registered all of them on time.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just be aware of the registration deadlines for the exams, but they re usually pretty long, around after the christmas break.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The compulsory modules were good, but the electives lacked a bit of quality.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: There were some rather demanding courses like "monitoring of forest resources", or bioclimatology. I enjoyed attending the lectures and studying together with my classmates in the library. The other courses also had an appropriate level, except of the electives. The ECTS there felt a little easier earned then in the compulsory modules.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was at times less intimate in Göttingen, i guess the style there is still a little more odl fashioned. I preferred the teaching style in Copenhagen, but i also got along really well with the lectures in Göttingen. We also had less assignments, since the entire semester is aimed towards the exams at the end, which are failry long and hard to study for. But all in all it was still a good experience, and i probably learned as much as i did in Copenhagen

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Monitoring of Forest Resources
2. Forest management under different climatic conditions
3. Bioclimatology and global change
4. Research planning
5. Ecological funtions of wildlife: implications for conservation and management

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: The second semester was reserved for the Master thesis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Monitoring of forest resources:
It really sharpens your mind and teaches you accuracy. You have to calculate and use logical thinking. It is by far the toughest, but for me the most rewarding subject even though the teaching style was a little strict, compared to what i was used from Copenhagen.
It is one of the few subjects that teaches some kind of statistics and that is essential in this field in my opinion.

Forest management under different climatic conditions:
This was a nice balance to monitoring, it was about applied silviculture, it included a bunch of excursions, and it was very visual and interactive, i really enjoyed this module

questions.answer: No items were more or less expensive than i expected. I think food is surprisingly cheap in Germany, also the cantines at the university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Through the university you can join many different sport clubs or get a membership for the gym or the swimming pools. The vaiety of available options was very big, and the fees very reasonable

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going to bars, and doing sports via unisport. A trip to the Harz mountains is always worth a visit, and it is not too far too.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking, going to bars, the library and doing sports.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I am German, so there were no Problems

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No challenges

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I like the high level of conscientiousness and the general accuracy/scrutiny in Germany

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get ready to write long written exams at the end of the semester. Study throughout the semester, because the exams will be in very short intervals. And try to keep up your relaxed temperament, germany is not so bad afterall

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing that i have not mentioned before.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Spending my days at library with my study group before the exams. I never had such a yielding studying experience, and i never benefitted that much from my classmates before.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greates challenge was the delay of my master thesis, other than that i was very focused on my studies and enjoeyed every bit of it

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
